article.headline: QQQ Call Skew Hits an All-Time High as AI Euphoria Peaks
article.lede: Options pricing on the Nasdaq-100 ETF has reached a historically extreme configuration: call skew at its all-time highest percentile while put skew sits at its all-time lowest, simultaneously. The data, drawn from Nomura's volatility desk and attributed to cross-asset macro strategist Charlie McElligott, was shared by the fintwit account @JoeyGEX. It is not a forecast but a positioning map — the market is running maximum-conviction long into mega-cap technology and artificial intelligence, with near-zero downside hedge, at the arithmetically most expensive moment in the recorded data to hold that view.
article.body:
*Options skew* describes how **implied volatility** — the market's expectation of future price swings, priced into options contracts — varies across strike prices at a given expiry. In normal equity markets, put options trade at a volatility premium to equivalent calls, because institutions chronically seek downside protection. The standard gauge is the **25-delta risk reversal**: the implied volatility of the 25-delta put minus the implied volatility of the 25-delta call, both for the same expiry. A 25-delta option sits roughly 10–15% out of the money on a three-month tenor — meaningful tail territory, not the catastrophic-tail range. When Nomura Holdings' (8604.T) charts show index skew at the 0th percentile, put skew at the 0th percentile, and call skew at the 100th percentile simultaneously, they are capturing the opposite of the market's normal configuration: downside protection has never been cheaper, and upside participation has never been more expensive. The 81st-percentile *at-the-money volatility* reading confirms this is not the complacency of a low-vol drift — absolute premiums are elevated — but all the directional bet is channeled into calls, with nothing left to hedge the other side.

Charlie McElligott, Nomura Holdings' managing director for cross-asset macro strategy, has spent a career translating options-dealer mechanics into macro narrative. His core concept is *dealer gamma exposure* (GEX): when dealers sell call options to clients, they must buy the underlying to *delta-hedge* the position; as the underlying rises, they must buy more to maintain that hedge, feeding the very rally that validates the original call buyers and draws in fresh demand. This reflexive loop is both a symptom and a partial cause of the extreme reading it documents — a 100th-percentile call skew is not simply a photograph of sentiment but itself a source of upward price pressure, at least while the loop remains intact.

The extreme arrived after a compressed, historically anomalous cycle. The April 2025 “Liberation Day” tariff shock sent the Nasdaq-100 down more than 10% in two sessions; the subsequent 90-day pause triggered the index's largest single-day gain since January 2001. A secondary correction in late March 2026 reversed in eleven trading sessions — the fastest oversold-to-overbought *RSI* reversal in the Nasdaq-100's 40-year history. Throughout, the AI infrastructure narrative remained intact: Apple (AAPL), Microsoft (MSFT), Alphabet (GOOGL), Amazon (AMZN), and Meta (META) committed more than $650 billion in aggregate AI capital expenditure, driving QQQ to record highs near $716 by mid-May 2026. Investors who missed either rally leg reached for out-of-the-money calls to catch up; those already long declined to hedge, confident the AI structural thesis justified an unprotected position.

The historical analogues are instructive if not precise. Cboe Global Markets (CBOE) data shows that retail call-buying into mega-cap technology names has reached its highest intensity since the 2021 meme-stock era — over 52% of retail opening activity in these stocks consisting of calls, at the 98th percentile of dispersion between index-implied volatility and single-stock implied volatility. The Nasdaq-100 peaked in November 2021 and fell roughly 33% into October 2022. The dot-com parallel is rougher but structurally legible: at the March 2000 peak, the seven largest Nasdaq-100 constituents held approximately 41% of index weight — essentially identical to the current combined weight of Apple (AAPL), Microsoft (MSFT), Nvidia (NVDA), Alphabet (GOOGL), Amazon (AMZN), Meta (META), and Tesla (TSLA) at approximately 41.7%. The Nasdaq-100 subsequently fell 78% over 30 months. SpotGamma, an options-analytics firm that has built its framework on McElligott's dealer-gamma concepts, noted that comparable call-skew extremes in Nvidia's options preceded stalling momentum in both November 2021 and June 2023.

A 100th-percentile reading is not a calendar date. Marquette Associates' analysis found that average one-month returns following spikes in the Cboe SKEW Index to the 90th percentile remain modestly positive — the loop can persist as long as each new buyer validates the one before. The signal is better read as a measure of **fragility**: the more crowded the long-call position, the more abrupt the unwind when a catalyst — an earnings miss, a macro shock, or exhaustion of the marginal buyer — severs the dealer-hedging feedback. Broadcom (AVGO), a key AI-chip supply-chain name that tracks the broader “Mag7+” cluster, saw its options behavior mirror this dynamic through the period, illustrating how deeply concentration risk runs through the index. What McElligott's data captures is a structure, not a trigger: maximum conviction, zero hedge, at the most expensive moment in this data set's history to express that view.

concepts.definition: The market's forward-looking estimate of how much an asset's price will swing, extracted from the price of an options contract. Higher implied volatility means options are more expensive. Unlike historical volatility, which looks backward, IV reflects what buyers and sellers currently expect — and is therefore a direct measure of market fear or greed at a given moment.

The pattern by which implied volatility differs across strike prices for options at the same expiry. In most equity markets, out-of-the-money puts carry higher IV than equivalent calls — a negative skew reflecting institutional demand for crash insurance. When skew inverts — calls more expensive than puts — it signals unusual demand for upside speculation relative to downside protection.

A standard skew measure: the difference in implied volatility between a 25-delta put and a 25-delta call at the same expiry. A 25-delta option has roughly a 25% probability of finishing in the money, placing it approximately 10–15% out of the money for a 3-month tenor on a large index. When this measure is near zero or inverted (calls more expensive than puts), the market is pricing upside risk more heavily than downside.

The implied volatility of options struck at or near the current price of the underlying asset. ATM vol is the market's most direct reading of expected near-term move magnitude, without the directional bias embedded in skew. At the 81st historical percentile, ATM vol is elevated — large moves are expected — but the skew data shows that those moves are being bet on overwhelmingly in one direction.

The aggregate of hedging obligations held by options market-makers (dealers) across all the contracts they have sold. When dealers carry net negative gamma — having sold more calls than they have bought — rising prices force them to buy the underlying to stay delta-neutral, amplifying the rally. Charlie McElligott of Nomura popularized this framework as a tool for explaining reflexive feedback loops in equity markets.

The practice by which options dealers continuously buy or sell the underlying asset to offset the directional exposure (delta) of the options they have written. Because delta changes as the underlying price moves, this hedging must be adjusted dynamically — and the aggregate of all dealers adjusting simultaneously can itself move prices, creating feedback effects independent of fundamental news.

The implied volatility of the 25-delta call relative to at-the-money implied volatility. High call skew means out-of-the-money calls are expensive relative to ATM options — a sign that participants are paying a premium to speculate on large upside moves. At the 100th historical percentile, call skew has never been higher in Nomura's dataset.

The implied volatility of the 25-delta put relative to at-the-money implied volatility. Low put skew means downside protection is cheap relative to ATM options. At the 0th historical percentile, put skew has never been lower — meaning the market has essentially stopped paying for crash insurance on the Nasdaq-100.

The informal label for the seven largest U.S. technology mega-caps — Apple, Microsoft, Nvidia, Alphabet, Amazon, Meta, and Tesla — coined by Bank of America analyst Michael Hartnett in 2023. The “plus” suffix extends the group to include AI-infrastructure adjacents such as Broadcom, AMD, and Taiwan Semiconductor. Together the core seven represent approximately 41.7% of QQQ's index weight, meaning their price action dominates the ETF's implied volatility.

A momentum oscillator that measures the speed and magnitude of recent price changes, producing a value between 0 and 100. Readings above 70 are conventionally overbought; below 30 is oversold. Technicians use it to gauge whether a move is extended relative to its own recent history. An RSI reversal from below 30 to above 70 in eleven sessions is, by historical comparison, extremely rapid.

The informal name for April 2, 2025, when President Trump announced sweeping reciprocal tariffs — a 10% global baseline and duties up to 50% on specific trading partners. The announcement triggered a sharp equity sell-off; a 90-day pause announced on April 9 triggered an immediate rebound, producing the largest single-day Nasdaq-100 gain since January 2001.

A ranking of the current implied volatility or skew reading against all prior readings in the dataset, expressed as a percentile. A 100th-percentile reading means the current value exceeds every prior observation in the history; 0th percentile means it is lower than all prior observations. Used to contextualize whether current options pricing is historically cheap, normal, or expensive.

ticker_8604-t.name: Nomura Holdings, Inc.
ticker_8604-t.blurb: Nomura Holdings is Japan's largest investment bank and brokerage firm, providing a broad range of financial services including retail brokerage, asset management, wholesale banking, and investment banking. Founded in 1925 and headquartered in Tokyo, it operates across Asia, Europe, and the Americas, serving individual investors, corporations, financial institutions, and governments. Nomura is widely regarded as the preeminent Japanese securities house and competes globally with major Western investment banks in fixed income, equities, and advisory services.
ticker_8604-t.recent: As of mid-May 2026, Nomura shares (8604.T) were trading around ¥1,265, near a 52-week low of ¥827 set on May 12, 2025, and well off the 52-week high of ¥1,506.50 reached in January 2026. Price action has been pressured by broader macro uncertainty including U.S.-China trade tensions and geopolitical headwinds affecting Asian financial markets. No company-specific earnings or major corporate announcements are surfaced in the available sources for the past 30 days.

ticker_aapl.name: Apple Inc.
ticker_aapl.blurb: Apple designs and markets consumer electronics (iPhone, Mac, iPad, Apple Watch), software, and digital services. The iPhone remains the dominant revenue driver, but the Services segment — comprising the App Store, Apple Music, iCloud, Apple Pay, and licensing — has grown into a high-margin business that Wall Street values separately. Apple commands one of the highest brand loyalty rates in consumer technology and operates a tightly integrated hardware-software ecosystem.
ticker_aapl.recent: Apple reported FY2025 revenue of approximately $400 billion. The company has faced headwinds from slowing iPhone upgrade cycles in mature markets and regulatory pressure on App Store commissions in both the US and EU. Apple Intelligence, its generative AI suite, launched in late 2024 but has not yet materially re-accelerated upgrade cycles. Paul Pelosi sold 45,000 shares of AAPL according to the January 2026 PTR disclosure — the largest single sale in the filing by share count.

sources.title: Nancy Pelosi Stock Tracker

ticker_msft.name: Microsoft Corporation
ticker_msft.description: Microsoft is a global software, cloud, and AI platform company. Its principal segments are Productivity and Business Processes (Office, LinkedIn, Dynamics), Intelligent Cloud (Azure, server products), and More Personal Computing (Windows, Xbox, Surface). The company is in a structural transition from a capital-light software licensor to a capital-intensive hyperscale cloud and AI infrastructure provider.
ticker_msft.blurb: Microsoft is a global software, cloud, and AI platform company. Its principal segments are Productivity and Business Processes (Office, LinkedIn, Dynamics), Intelligent Cloud (Azure, server products), and More Personal Computing (Windows, Xbox, Surface). The company is in a structural transition from a capital-light software licensor to a capital-intensive hyperscale cloud and AI infrastructure provider.
ticker_msft.recent: As of early May 2026, MSFT trades near $413 — down approximately 25.6% from its July 31, 2025 all-time high of $555.45 and -15.7% YTD — after touching a March 28 correction low of $356.07. The drawdown carried the stock briefly below its 200-week moving average for the first time in roughly 13 years (prior touches: 2009, 2018, 2020, 2022). Revenue grew 18% YoY with Azure +40%, while annualized AI revenue reached approximately $37 billion; calendar-2026 capex is projected near $190 billion and free cash flow contracted -22% YoY. Forward P/E is approximately 24.4.

ticker_googl.name: Alphabet Inc. (Class A)
ticker_googl.blurb: Alphabet is the parent company of Google, the world's dominant search engine, as well as YouTube, the Google Cloud Platform, and a portfolio of moonshot bets (Waymo, DeepMind, Verily). Search advertising accounts for the majority of revenue, but the cloud division has grown into a multi-billion-dollar profit centre. Alphabet is also a leading player in generative AI, having developed the Gemini family of large language models and integrated them across its product suite.
ticker_googl.recent: Alphabet reported FY2025 revenue of approximately $370 billion, with Google Cloud crossing $50 billion annually. The company has faced antitrust scrutiny in both the US and EU, with a US federal court ruling in 2024 that Google holds an illegal monopoly in general search. Despite regulatory headwinds, the stock has benefited from AI-driven search enhancements and strong cloud growth. Paul Pelosi exercised call options with a $150 strike (purchased January 2025, exercised January 2026) gaining approximately 75% over the period.

sources.title: Nancy Pelosi's 2026 Stock Moves — Motley Fool

ticker_amzn.name: Amazon.com, Inc.
ticker_amzn.blurb: Amazon operates the world's largest e-commerce marketplace and the leading cloud infrastructure platform, Amazon Web Services (AWS). AWS generates the majority of Amazon's operating profit despite representing a minority of total revenue. The company also has significant positions in digital advertising, streaming (Prime Video), and logistics infrastructure. Amazon is a major investor in AI, both through AWS cloud AI services and through a multi-billion-dollar strategic stake in Anthropic.
ticker_amzn.recent: Amazon reported FY2025 revenue exceeding $650 billion, with AWS growing at roughly 17% annually and crossing $100 billion in run-rate revenue. The advertising segment has become a meaningful profit contributor. Paul Pelosi exercised call options with a $150 strike (purchased January 2025, exercised January 2026), with the stock gaining approximately 10% over that period — the weakest performer in the Pelosi 2026 exercise batch.

sources.title: Nancy Pelosi's 2026 Stock Moves — Motley Fool

ticker_meta.name: Meta Platforms, Inc.
ticker_meta.blurb: Meta Platforms, headquartered in Menlo Park, California, operates Facebook, Instagram, WhatsApp, and Threads — collectively the largest social-media ecosystem in the world by monthly active users. The company generates the vast majority of its revenue through digital advertising, using detailed behavioural data to target ads across its platforms. After a painful 2022 in which shares fell roughly 65% amid a revenue slowdown and ballooning metaverse losses, Meta executed a dramatic turnaround by cutting costs, boosting margins, and rapidly integrating AI-driven ad ranking tools (Advantage+) that demonstrably improved advertiser returns. CEO Mark Zuckerberg declared 2023 a 'Year of Efficiency' and the company followed through. By late 2025 Meta was simultaneously the most profitable it had ever been and the most aggressive in AI infrastructure spending, committing up to $65 billion in capex for 2025 and raising that figure to as much as $145 billion for 2026.
ticker_meta.recent: Meta reached an all-time high near $796 per share in September 2025. The stock declined approximately 24–28% from that peak through April 2026, with the primary investor concern being the scale of the 2026 capital-expenditure commitment — up to $145 billion — and uncertainty about whether AI-driven revenue would materialise at the pace required to justify it. Quarterly earnings remained strong through the period, but multiple compression drove share-price weakness.

ticker_nvda.name: NVIDIA Corporation
ticker_nvda.blurb: NVIDIA designs graphics processing units (GPUs) and system-on-chip products. Originally a gaming chip company, it became the dominant supplier of AI accelerators — chips that perform the parallel matrix math required to train and run large language models. Its H100, H200, and Blackwell GPU families are the de facto standard for AI training infrastructure at hyperscalers and cloud providers. NVIDIA's CUDA software ecosystem creates deep switching costs: virtually all AI frameworks and models are optimised for CUDA, making competing hardware difficult to adopt at scale. NVIDIA also sells networking (InfiniBand, Ethernet) and data-centre systems.
ticker_nvda.recent: NVIDIA reported FY2026 (ending Jan 2026) revenue of $215.9 billion, up 65% YoY, with data centre revenue reaching $186 billion. The company's forward P/E of ~17.5x on 34.8% projected EPS growth produces a PEG of 0.50 — unusually cheap for what is arguably the most critical infrastructure company in the AI buildout. Hyperscalers (Microsoft, Amazon, Google, Meta) collectively committed over $200 billion in AI infrastructure capex for 2026, the majority flowing through NVIDIA's supply chain.

ticker_tsla.name: Tesla Inc.
ticker_tsla.blurb: Tesla designs and manufactures battery-electric vehicles, energy storage systems, and solar products. Founded in 2003 and taken public in June 2010 at seventeen dollars per share, it became one of the most spectacular long-term equity stories of the 2010s: every share from the IPO, adjusted for subsequent stock splits, would be worth roughly 6,500 dollars by late 2025 — a return of approximately 22,000 percent. The company's Model S (2012), Model 3 (2017), and Model Y (2020) progressively expanded the addressable market from luxury to mass-market segments. Tesla also operates a global Supercharger network and a large-scale energy storage division (Megapack). CEO Elon Musk's public profile — across social media, SpaceX, and his acquisition of X (formerly Twitter) — has made Tesla one of the more volatile large-cap equities in recent years, as investor sentiment toward the company has become partially indexed to sentiment toward Musk personally.
ticker_tsla.recent: Tesla has faced intensifying competition from Chinese electric-vehicle manufacturers, particularly BYD, which overtook Tesla in global EV sales in 2023. Revenue growth decelerated sharply in 2024, and the company has relied on price cuts to defend market share, compressing margins. Musk's political visibility during the 2024 US election cycle and his role in the DOGE cost-cutting initiative generated significant consumer backlash in some markets, with Tesla registrations declining in Europe and California in early 2025. The stock traded in a wide range through 2025-2026 as investors weighed the autonomous-vehicle (Full Self-Driving) optionality against near-term margin pressure.

ticker_avgo.name: Broadcom Inc.
ticker_avgo.blurb: Broadcom is a diversified semiconductor and infrastructure software company formed through a series of acquisitions, most recently VMware (closed 2023). Its chip portfolio spans networking ASICs (custom chips for hyperscaler AI clusters), enterprise storage controllers, WiFi silicon, and set-top-box processors. Broadcom's AI networking chips — particularly its Tomahawk Ethernet switching ASICs and custom AI accelerators built for Google, Meta, and Apple — have made it a second-tier AI infrastructure beneficiary behind NVIDIA. The VMware acquisition added high-margin enterprise software revenue that meaningfully improved the company's margin profile.
ticker_avgo.recent: Broadcom's FY2026 revenue (ending Oct 2026) is on track to exceed $65 billion, with AI-related chip revenue growing rapidly as hyperscalers expand custom silicon programs. Forward EPS growth of 56.3% and a forward P/E of ~23.4x produce a PEG of 0.42 — among the best risk-adjusted valuations in large-cap technology. CEO Hock Tan has guided to $60–90 billion in AI chip revenue by 2027 from three major hyperscaler customers alone.

ticker_cboe.name: Cboe Global Markets, Inc.
ticker_cboe.blurb: Cboe Global Markets is one of the world's largest exchange operators, providing trading in options, futures, equities, exchange-traded products (ETPs), foreign exchange, and multi-asset volatility products. The company is best known for operating the Chicago Board Options Exchange (CBOE) and the VIX volatility index, which is widely regarded as the market's 'fear gauge.' Cboe operates exchanges across North America, Europe, and Asia-Pacific, serving institutional and retail participants globally. Its data and access solutions segment provides a growing recurring revenue stream alongside its transaction-based exchange businesses.
